surface_source.quote: After completing the installation, we can now launch the Qwen-Code client via the qwen command from the terminal to complete the setup and connect to the locally served LLM.

agents.quote: However, I’ve been using local solutions for a while, too, to test things and because it somehow gives me joy to have and use a fully local setup (versus proprietary services).

also.quote: I can run both Codex (with the latest GPT model) and Qwen-Code with a local Qwen model side by side on the same machine without having to switch manually back and forth between models.

models.quote: If we accept the reported findings and risks (personally, I didn’t see any red flags), we can now proceed with the installation and hook up our local Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model to Qwen Code (and Codex and Claude Code in the next sections).

review_style.value: Wants to see what the agent is doing; writes the code he cares about himself
review_style.quote: I’m not quite there yet where I’m comfortable with that because maybe I’m a control freak, but I still like to see what’s going on.

also.quote: Today, I still write most of the code I care about myself. With “care about,” I mean in contexts where it matters that I understand the code and that the code is correct.

harness.value: Agents run on a separate DGX Spark; local models served by Ollama, tunnelled to the Mac over SSH
harness.quote: By the way, personally, I run my agents almost exclusively on my DGX Spark because I don’t want my Mac Mini to get too hot and I want to have the RAM available for other tasks.
